correctness.rationale: The mixed-distance table in the assigned proof was independently checked against the graph definition. If \(J\cap\{i-1,i\}=\varnothing\), the center \(z\) and spoke \(zx_i\) collide; if \(J\cap\{i-1,i+1\}=\varnothing\), the adjacent rim vertices collide, proving necessity. Under both conditions, the distinct local 0/1/2 patterns distinguish selected and omitted inserted vertices, rim vertices, spokes, and the two subdivided rim edges, proving sufficiency. Independently, direct BFS mixed-distance enumeration over every subset \(J\) for \(4\le n\le9\) found zero mismatches with the stated criterion. The all-\(n\) conclusion rests on the symbolic table, not this finite check. The cyclic packing omitting every third inserted index gives the bound, and exhaustive order-four checking confirms no two-landmark set works.
correctness.risk: The exact mixed metric dimension for all \(n\) is not claimed; only the inserted-landmark classification, universal upper bound and exact \(n=4\) case are established.

Such a uniform correction and structural characterization are mathematically useful even without determining the exact dimension for every \(n\).

final_claim: For the gear graph \(G_n\), \(n\ge4\), an inserted-vertex landmark set \(S_J=\{y_j:j\in J\}\) is mixed resolving exactly when \(J\cap\{i-1,i\}\ne\varnothing\) and \(J\cap\{i-1,i+1\}\ne\varnothing\) for every cyclic index \(i\). Hence omitted indices may be spaced at cyclic distance at least three, giving \(\operatorname{mdim}(G_n)\le\lceil2n/3\rceil<n\) for all \(n\ge4\), and \(\operatorname{mdim}(G_4)=3\).
limitations: The exhaustive checks through small \(n\) are corroborative only and do not establish the all-order bound.
